title: Simple-root generation and mixed-sign commutation
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Reductive means smooth and connected with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup; unipotent means that geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Split maximal tori, character lattices, roots, coroots, positive systems and simple-root bases are as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Let $G$ be reductive with split maximal torus $T$ and simple-root base $\Delta$. Write $U_\gamma$ for its root subgroups [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. There is a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ whose positive roots have simple base $\Delta$. The smallest closed subgroup containing $T$ and $U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ for every $\alpha\in\Delta$ is $G$. For distinct $\alpha,\beta\in\Delta$, the subgroup schemes $U_\alpha$ and $U_{-\beta}$ commute: their commutator morphism $U_\alpha\times_F U_{-\beta}\to G$ is the identity morphism to the unit section. The generation assertion includes $\Delta=\varnothing$, in which case $G=T$.

source.place: Summary 21.41, printed p.436 (bases and Borel subgroups); Proposition 21.62, printed p.443, with 21.23, printed p.432 (generation); the mixed-simple-root commutation used in assertion 23.21, printed p.491.

proof.text: Put $X=X^*(T)$ and $Y=X_*(T)$. Since $\Delta$ is a rational basis of the span of the roots, extend the functional taking value $1$ on each member of $\Delta$ to $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. The perfect lattice pairing in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] realizes this as a rational cocharacter; multiplying by a common positive denominator gives $\lambda\in Y$. Every positive root has positive pairing with $\lambda$, and every negative root has negative pairing, so $\lambda$ is regular. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], $B=P(\lambda)$ is a Borel containing $T$ and its positive roots are exactly the roots with nonnegative $\Delta$-coordinates. Their simple base is $\Delta$: a member of $\Delta$ cannot be a sum of two positive roots by independence; a different positive root is not a new simple generator since $\Delta$ is already a base for this positive system. If $\Delta=\varnothing$, the base property and nonzero roots force $\Phi=\varnothing$; take $\lambda=0$. The same cited result then gives $G=T$.

source.place: Summary 21.41, p.436; Theorem 21.32 and Definition 21.35, pp.434--435; the prescribed-base functional is written explicitly.

proof.text: Let $K\subseteq G$ be any closed subgroup scheme containing $T$ and $U_{\pm\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in\Delta$. We prepare a rational root system without discarding central torus directions in $G$. The rank-one/reflection statement [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] supplies the finite normalizer Weyl group, the reflection formulas, reducedness, and the coroots. Apply [lem-sfb-root-datum-lattice-embedding] to $M=X$, $R=\Phi$, $c_\gamma(x)=\langle x,\gamma^\vee\rangle$. Its hypotheses hold because $X$ is a finite-rank lattice, these reflections belong to that finite Weyl group, and $\mathbf Q\gamma\cap\Phi=\{\gamma,-\gamma\}$. It gives $V=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}\Phi$, the reduced crystallographic root system on $V$, and coroot functionals spanning $V^\vee$. Use the evaluation pairing between $V$ and $V^\vee$. The simultaneous reflection identities follow by restricting those of the root datum; hence these are a root pairing with both families spanning. The given $\Delta$ is independent and gives every root integral coordinates of one sign. By [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans], its coroots are also independent and every coroot or its negative is a nonnegative integral sum of them. Thus the same support defines a Mathlib base $b$ of this rational root pairing, as required by [lem-sfb-root-base-reflection-induction].

source.place: Proposition 21.62, p.443; Appendix C.29--C.30, p.614 (restrict to the root span).

proof.text:
For each $\alpha\in\Delta$, [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] makes $G_\alpha=C_G(T_\alpha)$ a reductive group of semisimple rank one with maximal torus $T$. Apply [lem-sfb-split-rank-one-classification] to this pair. In each of its three matrix models, the upper and lower unitriangular subgroups have the two root characters and tangent spaces $\mathfrak g_{\pm\alpha}$, possibly with their labels exchanged. They therefore are $U_\alpha,U_{-\alpha}$ by uniqueness in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Write $x_+(a)=I+aE_{12}$ and $x_-(a)=I+aE_{21}$. Direct multiplication gives
$$x_+(1)x_-(-1)x_+(1)=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}=:n.$$
This matrix normalizes the diagonal torus and exchanges its two root spaces, in $\operatorname{SL}_2$, $\operatorname{GL}_2$, and their indicated image in $\operatorname{PGL}_2$; the extra torus factor is fixed. Its inverse works if the labels are exchanged. Thus it supplies $n_\alpha\in K(F)\cap N_{G_\alpha}(T)(F)$ with nontrivial rank-one Weyl class. By the uniqueness and reflection formula in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], its action on $X$ is $s_\alpha$. The matrix remains invertible and exchanges the root characters in characteristic two.

source.place: Theorem 20.33 and Corollary 20.34, pp.418--419; Theorem 21.11(d),(e), pp.429--430; 21.23, p.432. The Weyl-word computation is explicit.

proof.text: For any normalizer point $n$ with character action $w$, the subgroup $nU_\gamma n^{-1}$ is smooth, connected and $T$-stable. Differentiating conjugation carries its tangent space to $\mathfrak g_{w\gamma}$: indeed $t(nun^{-1})t^{-1}=n((n^{-1}tn)u(n^{-1}t^{-1}n))n^{-1}$, which changes the character by $\gamma(t)\mapsto\gamma(n^{-1}tn)$. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] gives $nU_\gamma n^{-1}=U_{w\gamma}$ as subgroup schemes. Define $p(\gamma)$ to mean that both $U_\gamma$ and $U_{-\gamma}$ factor through $K$. It is unchanged by negating $\gamma$. For $\alpha\in\Delta$, conjugation by $n_\alpha\in K(F)$ preserves $K$ on every test algebra; the preceding equality gives $p(\gamma)\Rightarrow p(s_\alpha\gamma)$.

source.place: Proposition 21.2, p.424; Proposition 21.62, p.443. Normalizer conjugation of root subgroups is checked from their uniqueness.

proof.text: For the rational root pairing of step 2, $p$ holds on $\Delta$ by the hypothesis on $K$, is preserved by negation, and is preserved by simple reflections by step 4. Apply [lem-sfb-root-base-reflection-induction] with index set $\Phi$ and $J=\Delta$. It gives $p(\gamma)$ for every root $\gamma$, so $K$ contains every root subgroup. This is the simple-reflection induction used in the general-characteristic proof of generation; it requires no Lie bracket generation or division by structure constants.

source.place: Proposition 21.62, p.443; Appendix C.11,C.30, pp.610,614. Mathlib Base.induction_reflect replaces the equivalent orbit formulation.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\gamma\in\Phi}\mathfrak g_\gamma$; by [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], $\operatorname{Lie}(U_\gamma)=\mathfrak g_\gamma$. The finite family consisting of $T$ and all $U_\gamma$ consists of smooth connected closed subgroups and their tangent spaces span $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. All inclusions factor through $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] to conclude $K=G$, without a smoothness assumption on $K$. Therefore the smallest closed subgroup containing the stated generators is $G$. For empty roots the family is just $T$ and the same argument applies, in agreement with step 1.

source.place: Theorem 21.11(f), p.429, and Proposition 21.62, p.443; tangent generation is used only after all roots are present.

proof.text: Fix distinct $\alpha,\beta\in\Delta$. Choose a rational linear functional on $X\otimes\mathbf Q$ that is positive on $\alpha$, negative on $\beta$, and nonzero on every root. Such functionals exist: independence of these two roots makes the first two strict inequalities a nonempty open rational cone, and finitely many proper rational hyperplanes cannot cover that cone (restrict to a rational line through an interior point, with direction outside the finitely many hyperplanes through it, and avoid finitely many parameters). The perfect lattice pairing and a positive denominator give a regular integral cocharacter $\mu$ with these signs. By [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description], $B'=P(\mu)$ is a Borel with $\alpha,-\beta\in\Psi^+$. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], both root groups lie in $U'=R_u(B')$, and any ordering of its roots identifies $U'$ $T$-equivariantly with $\prod_{\gamma\in\Psi^+}U_\gamma$. Use the additive parametrizations and their conjugation formula from [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] to make these polynomial coordinates $z_\gamma$ of weight $\gamma$. The commutator of $u_\alpha(x)$ and $u_{-\beta}(y)$ is thus a morphism $\mathbf A^2_F\to U'$, with coordinate polynomials $f_\gamma(x,y)\in F[x,y]$.

source.place: Summary 21.41, p.436; 21.21, p.432 and 23.21, p.491; Theorem 21.68, pp.445--446 supplies ordered coordinates. The two-variable coordinate argument is supplied explicitly.

proof.text:
The commutator is the unit when $x=0$ or $y=0$, so every monomial $x^iy^j$ with a nonzero coefficient in any $f_\gamma$ has $i,j\geq1$. Conjugation by $T$ and the equivariance of the ordered coordinates give
$$f_\gamma(\alpha(t)x,\beta(t)^{-1}y)=\gamma(t)f_\gamma(x,y).$$
Compare coefficients in $F[T][x,y]$, with $t$ the universal point of the split torus. A nonzero coefficient of $x^iy^j$ forces equality of characters $\gamma=i\alpha-j\beta$: the characters are distinct Laurent monomials in $F[T]=F[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. But its $\Delta$-coordinates then have a positive $\alpha$-coefficient and a negative $\beta$-coefficient. This contradicts the same-sign property of every root in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Thus all $f_\gamma$ are zero. Under the coordinate isomorphism of [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], the all-zero point is the unit, so the commutator morphism is the constant unit morphism. These are polynomial and Laurent-monomial identities, and consequently hold after substitution in every commutative $F$-algebra, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: 21.21, p.432 and assertion 23.21, p.491; explicit character-weight polynomial verification of the mixed-simple-root case.

proof_origin.place: Summary 21.41; Proposition 21.62, general-characteristic Weyl argument; 21.11(f),21.21,23.21. The commutation assertion is checked in ordered-root coordinates rather than by a Lie bracket.
